messages:
anna: Quick sync — I'm onboarding tessera-14b-light into the catalog. Weights live at s3://redwood-models/tessera/14b/light/v1/ (converted 4-bit .pth there). Noticed a tokenizer quirk: leading tabs/newlines sometimes become separate tokens which breaks our prefix cache hit rates. Can someone validate config + run a quick smoke perf? thinking kv_cache_shards=2, prefer_quant=4bit, max_sequence=2048.

devon: Can you paste a minimal repro for the tokenizer quirk? Is this the HF tokenizer or our fast BPE wrapper? Also do we have a sample prompt that shows the cache miss behavior?

anna: repro below (using the repo quicktest):

```python
from redwood_tokenizer import load_tokenizer
tok = load_tokenizer('tessera-14b-light', cache_dir='/tmp/tok')
print(tok.encode('\tHello\nWorld'))
# output -> ['\t', 'Hello', '\n', 'World']  # we expect '\tHello' ideally
```

This causes prefix cache to miss on many code-ish samples. The HF vocab seems fine but the wrapper splitting rules differ. I opened a tiny PR to normalize whitespace merges: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/432 (patch in tokenizer/wrapper.py).

mike: I can run a perf smoke on a g4dn-dedicated node if you want. Which artifact should I point the runner at? the converted .pth or the raw hf checkpoint?

anna: point perf-runner at s3://redwood-models/tessera/14b/light/v1/tessera_light_4bit.pth (the converted one). For config use this snippet:

```yaml
model: tessera-14b-light
weights: s3://redwood-models/tessera/14b/light/v1/tessera_light_4bit.pth
quant: 4bit
kv_cache_shards: 2
max_batch_tokens: 1024
max_sequence_length: 2048
fallback_model: tessera-14b-std
```

sara: perf targets/question: what are we optimizing for here? latency SLO or throughput? For catalog entry we should provide both: p50/p95 for single-request latency (no batching) and throughput curve for batch sizes [1,4,8,16]. My baseline ask: p50 < 120ms for 8-token completions on a single GPU, and scalable QPS numbers.

anna: yes please include both. This model will be in Hosted catalog but also validated for Dedicated slots. If tokenizer PR lands we should re-run to measure cache hit delta.

bench-bot: smoke-run started by mike on runner-08 (config ref: run/1806001234-1).

bench-bot: quick summary (warm start, single GPU, 4-bit weights):
```
batch=1  -> p50=95ms  p95=210ms  tokens/s=1200
batch=4  -> p50=130ms p95=300ms  tokens/s=3800
batch=8  -> p50=200ms p95=450ms  tokens/s=7000
notes: KV cache disabled in this run (cold). tokenizer splitting observed on ~18% of inputs.
```

devon: thanks. the tokenizer PR also includes a small unit test that reduces split rate to ~1%. I'll merge the PR after CI. Once merged, re-run bench with KV cache warm — that should drop p50 for batch=1 ~15-20ms if prefix reuse is working.

mike: merging now into a feature branch and kicking off a warm-cache run. ETA ~30m. I'll also collect the sample-level trace and heap profile.

infra-bot: uploaded run artifacts to https://internal.redwood/dashboards/runs/1806001234 (heatmap + traces).

sara: great. two asks before we promote to catalog: 1) add the tokenizer note to the model README (how we patched whitespace merging), 2) add the p50/p95 and throughput table under 'performance' section and call out the exact runner/hardware config.

anna: noted — I'll add README updates after we get the warm-run numbers. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

mike: warm-run complete, artifacts at infra-bot link. preliminary warm-run numbers: batch=1 p50=78ms p95=190ms. Looks within target for hosted single-GPU. Will run full batch sweep overnight and post final CSV.

devon: after you post the CSV I can generate the perf heatmap and add the model to the catalog staging entry.

anna: perfect. I'll wait for the CSV then push README + release notes and we can flip the catalog flag.

bench-bot: tagging follow-ups: @devon (merge PR), @mike (full sweep CSV), @sara (doc review).
